# Weighted and unweighted polygenic score

Here we create a polygenic score consisting of the variance weighted averages of the target genes. We added _CD8B_ to the target list too.


## Prepare

Here we prepare a weighted and an unweighted polygenic score for the target genes. 

```{r}
library(SummarizedExperiment)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggpubr)

# Extract expression data from SummarizedExperiment
expression_data <- assay(AERNASE.targets)

# Ensure gene_list_qc is a character vector -- add CD8B
gene_list_qc <- as.character(gene_list_qc, "CD8B")

# Subset expression data for the target genes
expression_subset <- expression_data[rownames(expression_data) %in% gene_list_qc, , drop = FALSE]

# Check for missing genes
missing_genes <- setdiff(gene_list_qc, rownames(expression_subset))
if (length(missing_genes) > 0) {
  message("Warning: The following genes were not found in the dataset: ", paste(missing_genes, collapse = ", "))
}
```

We compute the variance and calculate the weights for the weighted score. 

```{r}
# Compute variance for each gene across individuals (rows)
gene_variance <- apply(expression_subset, 1, var, na.rm = TRUE)

# Normalize weights so they sum to 1
weights <- gene_variance / sum(gene_variance, na.rm = TRUE)

# Ensure weight vector matches number of selected genes
if (length(weights) != nrow(expression_subset)) {
  stop("Error: Weight vector length does not match the number of genes in the expression matrix.")
}
```

## Calculate scores

Now, we calculate the scores. 

```{r}
# Compute the variance-weighted polygenic score for each individual
weighted_score <- colSums(expression_subset * weights, na.rm = TRUE)

# Compute the unweighted polygenic score (mean expression per individual)
unweighted_score <- colMeans(expression_subset, na.rm = TRUE)

# Convert scores to a data frame
score_df <- data.frame(
  study_number = colnames(expression_subset),  # Match individuals (columns in expression data)
  weighted_score = weighted_score,  # Variance-weighted score
  unweighted_score = unweighted_score  # Unweighted mean expression score
)
```

We add the phenotype data to the score data for downstream analyses. 

```{r}
# Extract phenotype data from SummarizedExperiment (assumed in colData)
phenotype_data <- as.data.frame(colData(AERNASE.targets)) %>%
  dplyr::select(study_number, Fat.bin_10, SMC.bin, IPH.bin, Plaque_Vulnerability_Index)

# Merge phenotype data with scores
expression_phenotype <- inner_join(phenotype_data, score_df, by = "study_number")

# Add a factor for Plaque Vulnerability Index (PVI)
expression_phenotype$PVI_factor <- factor(expression_phenotype$Plaque_Vulnerability_Index, levels = as.character(0:5))
```

Here we perform some basic analyses and visualizations of the polygenic score.



Compute correlations.

```{r}

cor_results <- cor(expression_phenotype[, c("weighted_score", "unweighted_score", "Fat.bin_10", "SMC.bin", "IPH.bin", "Plaque_Vulnerability_Index")], 
                   use = "pairwise.complete.obs", method = "spearman")

# Print correlation results
```

### Visualizations

Let's visualize the correlations in a heatmap.

```{r}
library(pheatmap)
library(Hmisc)  # For rcorr() to get p-values

# Compute Spearman correlation with p-values
cor_results <- rcorr(as.matrix(expression_phenotype[, c("weighted_score", "unweighted_score", "Fat.bin_10", "SMC.bin", "IPH.bin", "Plaque_Vulnerability_Index")]), 
                     type = "spearman")

cor_matrix <- cor_results$r  # Extract correlation coefficients
p_matrix <- cor_results$P  # Extract p-values

# Rename variables and reorder rows/columns
new_names <- c("Fat", "SMCs", "IPH", "PVI", "Polygenic Score", "Unweighted Polygenic Score")

# Reorder the correlation matrix
cor_matrix <- cor_matrix[c("Fat.bin_10", "SMC.bin", "IPH.bin", "Plaque_Vulnerability_Index", "weighted_score", "unweighted_score"),
                         c("Fat.bin_10", "SMC.bin", "IPH.bin", "Plaque_Vulnerability_Index", "weighted_score", "unweighted_score")]

p_matrix <- p_matrix[c("Fat.bin_10", "SMC.bin", "IPH.bin", "Plaque_Vulnerability_Index", "weighted_score", "unweighted_score"),
                     c("Fat.bin_10", "SMC.bin", "IPH.bin", "Plaque_Vulnerability_Index", "weighted_score", "unweighted_score")]

# Apply new names
rownames(cor_matrix) <- new_names
colnames(cor_matrix) <- new_names

rownames(p_matrix) <- new_names
colnames(p_matrix) <- new_names

# Function to map p-values to asterisks
significance_levels <- function(p) {
  ifelse(p < 0.001, "***",
         ifelse(p < 0.01, "**",
                ifelse(p < 0.05, "*", "")))
}

# Generate asterisks for p-values
p_asterisks <- matrix(significance_levels(p_matrix), nrow = nrow(p_matrix), ncol = ncol(p_matrix))

# Remove diagonal values (set to empty string "")
diag(p_asterisks) <- ""

rownames(p_asterisks) <- new_names
colnames(p_asterisks) <- new_names

# Create the heatmap with asterisks
p <- pheatmap(cor_matrix, 
              cluster_rows = FALSE,
              cluster_cols = FALSE,
              color = colorRampPalette(c("blue", "white", "red"))(100), 
              fontsize = 12, 
              main = "Polygenic Score Correlation Heatmap",
              display_numbers = p_asterisks,  # Add asterisks for p-values
              number_color = "black")

# Save as PNG and PDF
ggsave(filename = paste0(PLOT_loc, "/", Today, ".", PROJECTNAME, ".polygenicscore_correlation_heatmap.png"), 
       plot = p[[4]], width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300)

ggsave(filename = paste0(PLOT_loc, "/", Today, ".", PROJECTNAME, ".polygenicscore_correlation_heatmap.pdf"), 
       plot = p[[4]], width = 8, height = 6)

# Cleanup
rm(p)
```


```{r}
library(tibble)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

# Function to compute correlation and p-values
compute_correlation_pval <- function(data, method = "spearman") {
  cor_matrix <- cor(data, use = "pairwise.complete.obs", method = method)  # Correlation matrix
  p_matrix <- matrix(NA, nrow = ncol(data), ncol = ncol(data), dimnames = list(colnames(data), colnames(data)))  # Empty p-value matrix
  
  for (i in 1:(ncol(data) - 1)) {
    for (j in (i + 1):ncol(data)) {
      test_result <- cor.test(data[[i]], data[[j]], method = method)  # Compute correlation
      p_matrix[i, j] <- test_result$p.value
      p_matrix[j, i] <- test_result$p.value  # Symmetric
    }
  }
  
  return(list(cor_matrix = cor_matrix, p_matrix = p_matrix))
}

# Compute correlation and p-values
cor_pval_results <- compute_correlation_pval(expression_phenotype[, c("weighted_score", "unweighted_score", "Fat.bin_10", "SMC.bin", "IPH.bin", "Plaque_Vulnerability_Index")])

# Convert correlation matrix to long format
cor_results_table <- as.data.frame(cor_pval_results$cor_matrix) %>%
  rownames_to_column(var = "Trait") %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -Trait, names_to = "Compared_With", values_to = "Correlation") %>%
  dplyr::filter(Trait != Compared_With)  # Remove self-correlations (diagonal)

# Convert p-value matrix to long format
pval_results_table <- as.data.frame(cor_pval_results$p_matrix) %>%
  rownames_to_column(var = "Trait") %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -Trait, names_to = "Compared_With", values_to = "p_value") %>%
  dplyr::filter(Trait != Compared_With)  # Remove self-correlations (diagonal)

# Merge correlation and p-value tables
cor_results_final <- inner_join(cor_results_table, pval_results_table, by = c("Trait", "Compared_With"))

# Format p-value column (e.g., "<0.001" for very small values)
cor_results_final$p_value <- ifelse(!is.na(cor_results_final$p_value) & cor_results_final$p_value < 0.001, 
                                    "<0.001", round(cor_results_final$p_value, 3))

# Export to CSV
write.csv(cor_results_final, file = paste0(OUT_loc, "/", Today, ".", PROJECTNAME, ".polygenicscore_correlation_results.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# Display table
print(cor_results_final)
```

```{r}
# Define NPG colors manually
npg_colors <- c("#E64B35", "#4DBBD5", "#00A087", "#3C5488", "#F39B7F", "#8491B4")

# Remove NA values
data_clean <- expression_phenotype %>% drop_na(PVI_factor, weighted_score)

# Convert factor to numeric for regression
data_clean$PVI_numeric <- as.numeric(data_clean$PVI_factor)

# Perform linear regression
lm_model <- lm(weighted_score ~ PVI_numeric, data = data_clean)
summary_lm <- summary(lm_model)

# Extract regression coefficient (β) and p-value
beta <- round(summary_lm$coefficients[2, 1], 3)  # Slope
p_value <- summary_lm$coefficients[2, 4]  # p-value

# Format p-value for display
p_text <- ifelse(p_value < 0.001, "p < 0.001", paste0("p = ", round(p_value, 3)))

# Create plot
p4 <- ggplot(data_clean, aes(x = PVI_numeric, y = weighted_score, color = PVI_factor)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.8) +  # Scatter points
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "black", aes(group = 1), linetype = "dashed") +  # Dotted regression line
  scale_color_manual(values = npg_colors) +  # Use manually defined NPG colors
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:length(levels(expression_phenotype$PVI_factor)),  # Ensure correct axis labels
                     labels = levels(expression_phenotype$PVI_factor)) +
  labs(title = "Polygenic Score vs PVI", x = "PVI", y = "Polygenic Score", color = "PVI") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = "white")) +  # White legend background
  annotate("text", x = max(data_clean$PVI_numeric) - 1, y = max(data_clean$weighted_score), 
           label = paste0("β = ", beta, ", ", p_text), 
           hjust = 1, size = 4, fontface = "bold")  # Add regression coefficient and p-value

p4  # Print the plot
```

# Module score

Let's use Seurat to create a module score for the target genes; a similar approach as presented in the NatCVR paper from [Mokry et al.](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44161-022-00171-0).

First, we will load `Seurat`. 

```{r}
library(Seurat)
```


## Create Seurat object
Next, we will create a Seurat object from the target genes.


For this we want to add the Gene Symbol to the rowdata of the `SummarizedExperiment`.
```{r}
library(SummarizedExperiment)

# Assume `rse` is your RangedSummarizedExperiment object
rse <- AERNASE  # Replace with your actual object

# Check available rowData columns
colnames(rowData(rse))

# Ensure the gene symbol column exists (adjust column name if needed)
if ("symbol" %in% colnames(rowData(rse))) {
  
  # Extract gene symbols and ENSG IDs
  gene_symbols <- rowData(rse)$symbol
  ensg_ids <- rownames(rse)
  
  # Replace missing gene symbols with "NoGeneName"
  gene_symbols[is.na(gene_symbols) | gene_symbols == ""] <- "NoGeneName"
  
  # Format as "Symbol_ENSG"
  new_gene_names <- paste0(gene_symbols, "_", ensg_ids)
  
  # Update rownames
  rownames(rse) <- new_gene_names
  
} else {
  warning("Gene Symbol column not found in rowData(rse). Check column names!")
}

# Check updated rownames
head(rownames(rse))

```


```{r}
# Create Seurat object using the RangedSummarizedExperiment dataset AERNASE.targets and including the associated metadata

# Extract count matrix
count_matrix <- assay(rse)  # Extract raw counts
dense_count_matrix <- as.matrix(count_matrix)  # Convert sparse to dense

# Extract metadata
metadata <- as.data.frame(colData(rse))  # Convert colData to a data frame

# Create a Seurat object
seurat_obj <- CreateSeuratObject(
  counts = dense_count_matrix, 
  meta.data = metadata,  # Attach metadata
  # min.cells = 3,         # Optional: Filter genes expressed in fewer than 3 cells
  # min.features = 200     # Optional: Filter cells with fewer than 200 detected genes
)

# Extract raw counts
raw_counts <- GetAssayData(seurat_obj, assay = "RNA", layer = "counts")

# Apply log-normalization: log1p() = log(1 + x) - we shouldn't use this, as the data are already vst-transformed
log_counts <- log1p(raw_counts)
dense_logcounts <- as.matrix(log_counts)  # Convert sparse to dense

# Add logcounts to the RNA assay in Seurat
seurat_obj[["RNA"]] <- SetAssayData(seurat_obj[["RNA"]], layer = "logcounts", new.data = dense_logcounts)

# Print summary of the Seurat object
print(seurat_obj)

# Verify logcounts is added
Layers(seurat_obj[["RNA"]])  # Check layers again

# rownames(seurat_obj)
rm(count_matrix, dense_count_matrix, log_counts, dense_logcounts, metadata)  # Remove temporary objects
```

### Adding module score to Seurat object

Now, let's add the module score to the Seurat object. Here we focus on these 4 genes: `RUNX3`, `PRDM1`, `GZMB`, and `CD3E`. The idea based on the correlation analyses and reflection on our single cell data was to focus on these genes. Conceptually this makes sense as, (for example) It’s entirely possible that `GNLY`, as an example, comes from a different cell type. Also upregulated `GZMB`, `RUNX3` and `PRDM1` are most consistent with what we observed in our single cell data - and so typing these to `CD3E` expression would be the ideal scenario.
We also add `CD8B` to the list of genes, as this is a marker for macrophages.


```{r}
# Define the target genes
sets <- list()
# sets$GSS <- c("RUNX3", "PRDM1", "GZMB", "CD3E")
sets$GMS <- c("RUNX3-ENSG00000020633", "PRDM1-ENSG00000057657", "GZMB-ENSG00000100453", "CD3E-ENSG00000198851")
sets$GMS_CD8B <- c("RUNX3-ENSG00000020633", "PRDM1-ENSG00000057657", "GZMB-ENSG00000100453", "CD3E-ENSG00000198851", "CD8B-ENSG00000172116")

# Check if genes exist in Seurat object
valid_genes <- intersect(sets$GMS, rownames(seurat_obj))
missing_genes <- setdiff(sets$GMS, rownames(seurat_obj))

valid_genes_CD8B <- intersect(sets$GMS_CD8B, rownames(seurat_obj))
missing_genes_CD8B <- setdiff(sets$GMS_CD8B, rownames(seurat_obj))

# Check if genes exist in Seurat object
if (length(missing_genes) > 0) {
  message("Warning: The following genes are not found in Seurat object: ", paste(missing_genes, collapse = ", "))
} else {
  message("All genes found in Seurat object.")
}

```


### Calculate module score

Setup the `GeneModuleScore` function to compute the module score.

```{r}
library(Matrix)

GeneModuleScore <- function(seurat_obj, gene_set, name = "ModuleScore", assay = "RNA", layer = "ounts", ctrl = 50, seed = 42) {
  
  set.seed(seed)  # Ensure reproducibility

  # Extract data from Seurat object
  expression_matrix <- GetAssayData(seurat_obj, assay = assay, layer = layer)
  
  # Ensure the gene set exists in the expression data
  valid_genes <- intersect(gene_set, rownames(expression_matrix))
  missing_genes <- setdiff(gene_set, rownames(expression_matrix))
  
  if (length(valid_genes) == 0) {
    stop("Error: No valid genes found in Seurat object. Cannot compute module score.")
  }
  
  if (length(missing_genes) > 0) {
    message("Warning: The following genes were not found: ", paste(missing_genes, collapse = ", "))
  }
  
  # Compute mean expression of selected genes per cell
  target_score <- colMeans(expression_matrix[valid_genes, , drop = FALSE])

  # Compute average expression of all genes to determine bins
  avg_expression <- rowMeans(expression_matrix)

  # Bin genes based on expression level
  expression_bins <- cut_number(avg_expression, n = 24, labels = FALSE, right = FALSE)
  names(expression_bins) <- names(avg_expression)

  # Select control genes from the same expression bins
  control_genes <- vector(mode = "list", length = length(valid_genes))
  
  for (i in seq_along(valid_genes)) {
    gene_bin <- expression_bins[valid_genes[i]]
    bin_genes <- names(expression_bins[expression_bins == gene_bin])
    
    # Exclude the original gene and take a random subset of control genes
    control_genes[[i]] <- setdiff(bin_genes, valid_genes[i])
    
    if (length(control_genes[[i]]) >= ctrl) {
      control_genes[[i]] <- sample(control_genes[[i]], size = ctrl, replace = FALSE)
    }
  }
  
  # Flatten the list and remove duplicates
  control_genes <- unique(unlist(control_genes))
  
  if (length(control_genes) == 0) {
    stop("Error: No valid control genes found.")
  }
  
  # Compute mean expression of control genes
  control_score <- colMeans(expression_matrix[control_genes, , drop = FALSE])

  # Compute module score as the difference
  module_score <- target_score - control_score

  # Store module score in Seurat metadata
  seurat_obj@meta.data[[name]] <- module_score

  message("Successfully added module score: ", name)
  
  return(seurat_obj)
}
```

Compute the module score. We also add the score including _CD8B_.

```{r}
# Add module score to Seurat object
seurat_obj <- GeneModuleScore(seurat_obj, gene_set = sets$GMS, name = "GMS", assay = "RNA", layer = "counts", ctrl = 50)

seurat_obj <- GeneModuleScore(seurat_obj, gene_set = sets$GMS_CD8B, name = "GMS_CD8B", assay = "RNA", layer = "counts", ctrl = 50)
```

# GMS in relation to plaque phenotypes

Let's plot the Gene Module Score (GMS) for our targets.


## GMS vs PVI

```{r}
# Load necessary library
library(ggpubr)

# Filter metadata_df to remove NA values
metadata_df_clean <- metadata_df %>% dplyr::filter(!is.na(Plaque_Vulnerability_Index))

# Add a factor for Plaque Vulnerability Index (PVI)
metadata_df_clean$PVI_factor <- factor(metadata_df_clean$Plaque_Vulnerability_Index, levels = as.character(0:5))
metadata_df$PVI_factor <- factor(metadata_df$Plaque_Vulnerability_Index, levels = as.character(0:5))

# Compute correlation (Spearman is recommended for ordinal/categorical PVI)
cor_test <- cor.test(as.numeric(metadata_df_clean$Plaque_Vulnerability_Index), metadata_df_clean$GMS, method = "spearman")

# Extract correlation coefficient (R) and p-value
r_value <- cor_test$estimate
r_squared <- r_value^2  # Compute R²
p_value <- cor_test$p.value

# Create correlation text label
cor_label <- paste0("R² = ", round(r_squared, 3), "\n p = ", signif(p_value, 3))

# Add comparison per group
my_comparisons <- list( c("0", "1"), c("0", "2"), c("0", "3"), c("0", "4"), c("0", "5")   )
```

### Visualize GMS

```{r}
# Create a boxplot of the module score
p_box <- ggboxplot(metadata_df_clean, 
                   x = "PVI_factor", 
                   y = "GMS", 
                   add = "jitter", 
                   color = "PVI_factor", 
                   palette = "npg",
                   ylim = c(-1.25, 2)) +
  # stat_compare_means(comparisons = my_comparisons, label = "p.signif") + # Add pairwise comparisons
  # stat_compare_means(label.y = 0.55) +  # Global p-value
  labs(title = "Gene Module Score vs PVI", 
       x = "PVI", 
       y = "Gene Module Score",
       color = "PVI") + 
  annotate("text", 
           x = 4.5, 
           y = 1.75,
           label = cor_label, 
           size = 5, hjust = 0) +
  theme_minimal()

p_box
```

```{r}
# Create the boxplot with jitter and regression line

       y = "Gene Module Score",

  annotate("text", x = 4.5, y = 1.75, label = cor_label, size = 5, hjust = 0) +  # R²
  scale_color_npg(na.value = "grey") +  # Set NA to grey
```

```{r}
# Define NPG colors manually
npg_colors <- c("#E64B35", "#4DBBD5", "#00A087", "#3C5488", "#F39B7F", "#8491B4")

# Remove NA values
data_clean <- metadata_df %>% drop_na(PVI_factor, GMS)

# Convert factor to numeric for regression
data_clean$PVI_numeric <- as.numeric(data_clean$PVI_factor)

# Perform linear regression
lm_model <- lm(GMS ~ PVI_numeric, data = data_clean)
summary_lm <- summary(lm_model)

# Extract regression coefficient (β) and p-value
beta <- round(summary_lm$coefficients[2, 1], 3)  # Slope
p_value <- summary_lm$coefficients[2, 4]  # p-value

# Format p-value for display
p_text <- ifelse(p_value < 0.001, "p < 0.001", paste0("p = ", round(p_value, 3)))
```


```{r}
# Create plot
p4 <- ggplot(data_clean, aes(x = PVI_numeric, y = GMS, color = PVI_factor)) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2, size = 3, alpha = 0.8) +  # Add jitter to prevent overlap
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.8) +  # Scatter points
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "black", aes(group = 1), linetype = "dashed") +  # Dotted regression line
  scale_color_manual(values = npg_colors) +  # Use manually defined NPG colors
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:length(levels(expression_phenotype$PVI_factor)),  # Ensure correct axis labels
                     labels = levels(expression_phenotype$PVI_factor)) +
  labs(title = "Polygenic Score vs PVI", x = "PVI", y = "Polygenic Score", color = "PVI") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = "white")) +  # White legend background
  annotate("text", x = max(data_clean$PVI_numeric), y = max(data_clean$GMS), 
           label = paste0("β = ", beta, ", ", p_text), 
           hjust = 1, size = 4, fontface = "bold")  # Add regression coefficient and p-value

p4  # Print the plot
```

## Covariates & other variables

1.  Age (continuous in 1-year increment). [`Age`]
2.  Sex (male vs. female). [`Gender`]
3.  Presence of hypertension at baseline (defined either as history of hypertension, SBP ≥140 mm Hg, DBP ≥90 mm Hg, or prescription of antihypertensive medications). [`Hypertension.composite`]
4.  Presence of diabetes mellitus at baseline (defined either as a history of diabetes and/or administration of glucose lowering medication). [`DiabetesStatus`]
5.  Smoking (current, ex-, never). [`SmokerStatus`]
6.  LDL-C levels (continuous). [`LDL_final`]
7.  Use of lipid-lowering drugs. [`Med.Statin.LLD`]
8.  Use of antiplatelet drugs. [`Med.all.antiplatelet`]
9.  eGFR (continuous). [`GFR_MDRD`]
10.	BMI (continuous). [`BMI`]
11.	History of cardiovascular disease (stroke, coronary artery disease, peripheral artery disease). [`MedHx_CVD`] combination of [`CAD_history`, `Stroke_history`, `Peripheral.interv`]
12.	Level of stenosis (50-70% vs. 70-99%). [`stenose`]
13. Year of surgery [`ORdate_year`] as we discovered in Van Lammeren _et al._ the composition of the plaque and therefore the Athero-Express Biobank Study has changed over the years. Likely through changes in lifestyle and primary prevention regimes.

## Models

We will analyze the data through four different models

- Model 1: adjusted for age, sex, and year of surgery
- Model 2: adjusted for age, sex, year of surgery, and additionally adjusted for history hypertension (defined from medical history and/or use of antihypertensive medications), diabetes (defined as history of a diagnosis and/or use of glucose-lowering medications), current smoking, LDL-C levels at time of operation, use of statins, use of antiplatelet agents, eGFR, BMI, history of cardiovascular disease (coronary artery disease, stroke, peripheral artery disease), and level of stenosis (50-70%, 70-90%, 90-99%)

## A. Cross-sectional analysis plaque phenotypes

In the cross-sectional analysis of plaque `r TRAIT_OF_INTEREST` levels we will focus on the following plaque vulnerability phenotypes:

- Percentage of macrophages (continuous trait)
- Percentage of SMCs (continuous trait)
- Number of intraplaque microvessels per 3-4 hotspots (continuous trait)
- Presence of moderate/heavy calcifications (binary trait)
- Presence of moderate/heavy collagen content (binary trait)
- Presence of lipid core no/<10% vs. >10% (binary trait)
- Presence of intraplaque hemorrhage (binary trait)


First, we need to add a few variables to the metadata.
```{r}
# Rename Seurat object

AERNAseurat <- seurat_obj
rm(seurat_obj, metadata_df)
```

We'll add the following variables to the metadata:

- `dateok`
- `MedHx_CVD`


```{r}
# Add dateok of surgery to metadata
AERNAseurat@meta.data$dateok <- AEDB.CEA$dateok[match(rownames(AERNAseurat@meta.data), AEDB.CEA$STUDY_NUMBER)]

# Add DiabetesStatus
AERNAseurat@meta.data$MedHx_CVD <- AEDB.CEA$MedHx_CVD[match(rownames(AERNAseurat@meta.data), AEDB.CEA$STUDY_NUMBER)]
```


```{r}
AERNAseurat@meta.data$MAC_SMC_ratio_rank  <- qnorm((rank(AERNAseurat@meta.data$MAC_SMC_ratio, na.last = "keep") - 0.5) / sum(!is.na(AERNAseurat@meta.data$MAC_SMC_ratio)))
```

### Model 1

In this model we correct for _Age_, _Gender_, and _year of surgery_.

Here we use the inverse-rank normalized data - visually this is more normally distributed.

#### Quantitative plaque traits

```{r}
detach("package:EnsDb.Hsapiens.v86", unload = TRUE)
detach("package:ensembldb", unload = TRUE)

```

Analysis of continuous/quantitative plaque traits as a function of plaque `r TRAIT_OF_INTEREST` expression levels.

```{r CrossSec: plaques - linear regression MODEL1 RANK, paged.print=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(MASS)

GLM.results <- data.frame(matrix(NA, ncol = 15, nrow = 0))

cat("Running linear regression...\n")
for (target_of_interest in 1:length(TRAITS.TARGET.RANK)) {
  TARGET = TRAITS.TARGET.RANK[target_of_interest]
  cat(paste0("\nAnalysis of ",TARGET,".\n"))
  for (trait in 1:length(TRAITS.CON.RANK)) {
    TRAIT = TRAITS.CON.RANK[trait]
    cat(paste0("\n- processing ",TRAIT,"\n\n"))
    currentDF <- as.data.frame(AERNAseurat_meta %>%
      dplyr::select(., TARGET, TRAIT, COVARIATES_M1) %>%
      filter(complete.cases(.))) %>%
      filter_if(~is.numeric(.), all_vars(!is.infinite(.)))
    # # for debug
    # print(DT::datatable(currentDF))
    # print(nrow(currentDF))
    # print(str(currentDF))
    ### univariate
    # fit <- lm(currentDF[,TARGET] ~ currentDF[,TRAIT] + Age + Gender + ORdate_year, data = currentDF)
    fit <- lm(currentDF[,TARGET] ~ currentDF[,TRAIT] + Age + Gender + ORdate_epoch, data = currentDF)
    model_step <- stepAIC(fit, direction = "both", trace = FALSE)
    # print(model_step)
    # print(summary(fit))

    GLM.results.TEMP <- data.frame(matrix(NA, ncol = 15, nrow = 0))
    GLM.results.TEMP[1,] = GLM.CON(fit, "AERNAseurat_meta", TARGET, TRAIT, verbose = TRUE)
    GLM.results = rbind(GLM.results, GLM.results.TEMP)
  }
}
cat("Edit the column names...\n")
colnames(GLM.results) = c("Dataset", "Predictor", "Trait",
                          "Beta", "s.e.m.",
                          "OR", "low95CI", "up95CI",
                          "T-value", "P-value", "r^2", "r^2_adj", "N", "Model_N", "Perc_Miss")

cat("Correct the variable types...\n")
GLM.results$Beta <- as.numeric(GLM.results$Beta)
GLM.results$s.e.m. <- as.numeric(GLM.results$s.e.m.)
GLM.results$OR <- as.numeric(GLM.results$OR)
GLM.results$low95CI <- as.numeric(GLM.results$low95CI)
GLM.results$up95CI <- as.numeric(GLM.results$up95CI)
GLM.results$`T-value` <- as.numeric(GLM.results$`T-value`)
GLM.results$`P-value` <- as.numeric(GLM.results$`P-value`)
GLM.results$`r^2` <- as.numeric(GLM.results$`r^2`)
GLM.results$`r^2_adj` <- as.numeric(GLM.results$`r^2_adj`)
GLM.results$`N` <- as.numeric(GLM.results$`N`)
GLM.results$`Model_N` <- as.numeric(GLM.results$`Model_N`)
GLM.results$`Perc_Miss` <- as.numeric(GLM.results$`Perc_Miss`)

# Save the data
cat("Writing results to Excel-file...\n")
### Univariate
library(openxlsx)
write.xlsx(GLM.results,
           file = paste0(OUT_loc, "/",Today,".AERNAseurat_meta.Con.Uni.",TRAIT_OF_INTEREST,".PlaquePhenotypes.RANK.MODEL1.xlsx"),
           rowNames = FALSE, colNames = TRUE, sheetName = "Con.Uni.PlaquePheno")

# Removing intermediates
cat("Removing intermediate files...\n")
rm(TRAIT, trait, currentDF, GLM.results, GLM.results.TEMP, fit, model_step)


```


### Model 2

In this model we correct for _Age_, _Gender_, _year of surgery_, _Hypertension status_, _Diabetes status_, _current smoker status_, _lipid-lowering drugs (LLDs)_, _antiplatelet medication_, _eGFR (MDRD)_, _BMI_, _MedHx_CVD_ (combination of _CAD history_, _stroke history_, and _peripheral interventions_), and _stenosis_.

Here we use the `inverse-rank normalized` data - visually this is more normally distributed.

#### Quantitative plaque traits

Analysis of continuous/quantitative plaque traits as a function of plaque `r TRAIT_OF_INTEREST` expression levels.

## Target expression vs. vulnerability index

We will also correlate the target levels to the `Plaque vulnerability index`. First, we'll visualize this, next we run model 1 and model 2. 

### Visualize

Here we plot the target levels to the `Plaque vulnerability index`. 

```{r Fix ORyearGroup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(sjlabelled)

AERNAseurat_meta$yeartemp <- as.numeric(year(AERNAseurat_meta$dateok))

attach(AERNAseurat_meta)

AERNAseurat_meta[,"ORyearGroup"] <- NA
AERNAseurat_meta$ORyearGroup[yeartemp <= 2007] <- "< 2007"
AERNAseurat_meta$ORyearGroup[yeartemp > 2007] <- "> 2007"
detach(AERNAseurat_meta)

table(AERNAseurat_meta$ORyearGroup, AERNAseurat_meta$ORdate_year)
```


```{r per PlaqueVulnerabilityIndex}

cat(paste0("Processing gene: \n"))
gene_module_list <- c("GMS", "GMS_CD8B")
for (TARGET_GENE in gene_module_list) {

  cat(paste0("- ", TARGET_GENE, "\n"))

  compare_means(as.formula(paste0(TARGET_GENE, " ~ Plaque_Vulnerability_Index")),  data = AERNAseurat_meta, method = "kruskal.test")
  p1 <- ggpubr::ggboxplot(AERNAseurat_meta, 
                    x = "Plaque_Vulnerability_Index",
                    y = TARGET_GENE,  
                    xlab = "Plaque vulnerability index",
                    ylab = paste0(TARGET_GENE, " (normalized expression)\n"),
```

```{r CrossSec: Plaque_Vulnerability_Index - ordinal regression MODEL1 RANK, paged.print=TRUE}

cat(paste0("Processing gene: \n"))
```

## B. Cross-sectional analysis symptoms

We will perform a cross-sectional analysis between plaque `r TRAIT_OF_INTEREST` expression levels and the 'clinical status' of the plaque in terms of presence of patients' symptoms (symptomatic vs. asymptomatic). The symptoms of interest are:

- stroke
- TIA
- retinal infarction
- amaurosis fugax
- asymptomatic

### Model 1

In this model we correct for _Age_, _Gender_, and _year of surgery_.

```{r CrossSec: symptoms - logistic regression MODEL1 RANK}
library(MASS)
GLM.results <- data.frame(matrix(NA, ncol = 16, nrow = 0))

    cat(paste0("\n- processing ",TRAIT,"\n\n"))
    currentDF <- as.data.frame(AERNAseurat_meta %>%
      dplyr::select(., TARGET, TRAIT, COVARIATES_M1) %>%
```

## C. Longitudinal analysis secondary clinical outcome

For the longitudinal analyses of plaque `r TRAIT_OF_INTEREST` expression levels and secondary cardiovascular events over a three-year follow-up period. 

The _primary outcome_ is defined as "a composite of fatal or non-fatal myocardial infarction, fatal or non-fatal stroke, ruptured aortic aneurysm, fatal cardiac failure, coronary or peripheral interventions, leg amputation due to vascular causes, and cardiovascular death", i.e. major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Variable: `epmajor.3years`, these include:
- myocardial infarction (MI)
- cerebral infarction (CVA/stroke)
- cardiovascular death (exact cause to be investigated)
- cerebral bleeding (CVA/stroke)
- fatal myocardial infarction (MI)
- fatal cerebral infarction
- fatal cerebral bleeding
- sudden death
- fatal heart failure
- fatal aneurysm rupture
- other cardiovascular death..

The _secondary outcomes_ will be 

- incidence of fatal or non-fatal stroke (ischemic and bleeding) - variable: `epstroke.3years`, these include:
  - cerebral infarction (CVA/stroke)
  - cerebral bleeding (CVA/stroke)
  - fatal cerebral infarction
  - fatal cerebral bleeding.
- incidence of acute coronary events (fatal or non-fatal myocardial infarction, coronary interventions) - variable: `epcoronary.3years`, these include:
  - myocardial infarction (MI)
  - coronary angioplasty (PCI/PTCA)
  - cardiovascular death (exact cause to be investigated)
  - coronary bypass (CABG)
  - fatal myocardial infarction (MI)
  - sudden death.
- cardiovascular death - variable: `epcvdeath.3years`, these include:
  - cardiovascular death (exact cause to be investigated)
  - fatal myocardial infarction (MI)
  - fatal cerebral infarction
  - fatal cerebral bleeding
  - sudden death
  - fatal heart failure
  - fatal aneurysm rupture
  - other cardiovascular death..


```{r}

                                                        "ep_cvdeath_t_3years",
                                                        "epstroke.3years", "epcoronary.3years", "epcvdeath.3years"
                                                        )),
```

### Sanity checks

First we do some sanity checks and inventory the time-to-event and event variables.
```{r Cox-regressions: General}
# Reference: https://bioconductor.org/packages/devel/bioc/vignettes/MultiAssayExperiment/inst/doc/QuickStartMultiAssay.html
# If you want to suppress warnings and messages when installing/loading packages
# suppressPackageStartupMessages({})

cat("* Creating function to summarize Cox regression and prepare container for results.")
# Function to get summary statistics from Cox regression model
COX.STAT <- function(coxfit, DATASET, OUTCOME, target_of_interest){
  cat("Summarizing Cox regression results for '", target_of_interest ,"' and its association to '",OUTCOME,"' in '",DATASET,"'.\n")
  if (nrow(summary(coxfit)$coefficients) == 1) {
    output = c(target_of_interest, rep(NA,8))
    cat("Model not fitted; probably singular.\n")
  }else {
    cat("Collecting data.\n\n")
    cox.sum <- summary(coxfit)
    cox.effectsize = cox.sum$coefficients[1,1]
    cox.SE = cox.sum$coefficients[1,3]
    cox.HReffect = cox.sum$coefficients[1,2]
    cox.CI_low = exp(cox.effectsize - 1.96 * cox.SE)
    cox.CI_up = exp(cox.effectsize + 1.96 * cox.SE)
    cox.zvalue = cox.sum$coefficients[1,4]
    cox.pvalue = cox.sum$coefficients[1,5]
    cox.sample_size = cox.sum$n
    cox.nevents = cox.sum$nevent
    
    output = c(DATASET, OUTCOME, target_of_interest, cox.effectsize, cox.SE, cox.HReffect, cox.CI_low, cox.CI_up, cox.zvalue, cox.pvalue, cox.sample_size, cox.nevents)
    cat("We have collected the following:\n")
    cat("Dataset used..............:", DATASET, "\n")
    cat("Outcome analyzed..........:", OUTCOME, "\n")
    cat("Protein...................:", target_of_interest, "\n")
    cat("Effect size...............:", round(cox.effectsize, 6), "\n")
    cat("Standard error............:", round(cox.SE, 6), "\n")
    cat("Odds ratio (effect size)..:", round(cox.HReffect, 3), "\n")
    cat("Lower 95% CI..............:", round(cox.CI_low, 3), "\n")
    cat("Upper 95% CI..............:", round(cox.CI_up, 3), "\n")
    cat("T-value...................:", round(cox.zvalue, 6), "\n")
    cat("P-value...................:", signif(cox.pvalue, 8), "\n")
    cat("Sample size in model......:", cox.sample_size, "\n")
    cat("Number of events..........:", cox.nevents, "\n")
  }
  return(output)
  print(output)
}
```

### Cox regressions

Let's perform the actual Cox-regressions. We will apply a couple of models: 

- Model 1: adjusted for age, sex, and year of surgery
- Model 2: adjusted for age, sex, year of surgery, hypertension, diabetes, smoking, LDL-C levels, lipid-lowering drugs, antiplatelet drugs, eGFR, BMI, history of CVD, level of stenosis

#### 3 years follow-up

##### Model 1
```{r Cox-regression Analysis: Simple model}
# Set up a dataframe to receive results
COX.results <- data.frame(matrix(NA, ncol = 12, nrow = 0))

# Looping over each target_of_interest/endpoint/time combination
for (i in 1:length(times)){
  eptime = times[i]
  ep = endpoints[i]
  cat(paste0("* Analyzing the effect of plaque target-of-interest on [",ep,"].\n"))
  cat(" - creating temporary SE for this work.\n")
  TEMP.DF = as.data.frame(AERNAseurat_meta_cox)
  cat(" - making a 'Surv' object and adding this to temporary dataframe.\n")
  TEMP.DF$event <- as.integer(TEMP.DF[,ep])
  TEMP.DF$y <- Surv(time = TEMP.DF[,eptime], event = TEMP.DF$event)
  cat(" - making strata of each of the plaque target-of-interest and start survival analysis.\n")
  
  for (target_of_interest in 1:length(TRAITS.TARGET.RANK)){
    cat(paste0("   > processing [",TRAITS.TARGET.RANK[target_of_interest],"]; ",target_of_interest," out of ",length(TRAITS.TARGET.RANK)," target-of-interest.\n"))
    # splitting into two groups
    TEMP.DF[[ TRAITS.TARGET.RANK[target_of_interest] ]] <- cut2(TEMP.DF[,TRAITS.TARGET.RANK[target_of_interest]], g = 2)
    cat(paste0("   > cross tabulation of ",TRAITS.TARGET.RANK[target_of_interest],"-stratum.\n"))
    show(table(TEMP.DF[[ TRAITS.TARGET.RANK[target_of_interest] ]]))
    
    cat(paste0("\n   > fitting the model for ",TRAITS.TARGET.RANK[target_of_interest],"-stratum.\n"))
    fit <- survfit(as.formula(paste0("y ~ ", TRAITS.TARGET.RANK[target_of_interest])), data = TEMP.DF)
    
    cat(paste0("\n   > make a Kaplan-Meier-shizzle...\n"))
    # make Kaplan-Meier curve and save it
    show(ggsurvplot(fit, data = TEMP.DF,
                    palette = c("#DB003F", "#1290D9"),
                    # palete = c("F59D10", "#DB003F", "#49A01D", "#1290D9"),
                    linetype = c(1,2),
                    # linetype = c(1,2,3,4),
                    # conf.int = FALSE, conf.int.fill = "#595A5C", conf.int.alpha = 0.1,
                    pval = FALSE, pval.method = FALSE, pval.size = 4,
                    risk.table = TRUE, risk.table.y.text = FALSE, tables.y.text.col = TRUE, fontsize = 4,
                    censor = FALSE,
                    legend = "right",
                    legend.title = paste0("",TRAITS.TARGET.RANK[target_of_interest],""),
                    legend.labs = c("low", "high"),
                    title = paste0("Risk of ",ep,""), xlab = "Time [years]", font.main = c(16, "bold", "black")))
    dev.copy2pdf(file = paste0(COX_loc,"/",
                               Today,".AERNAseurat_meta.survival.",ep,".2G.",
                               TRAITS.TARGET.RANK[target_of_interest],".pdf"), width = 12, height = 10, onefile = FALSE)

    cat(paste0("\n   > perform the Cox-regression fashizzle and plot it...\n"))
    ### Do Cox-regression and plot it
    
    ### MODEL 1 (Simple model)
    cox = coxph(Surv(TEMP.DF[,eptime], event) ~ TEMP.DF[[ TRAITS.TARGET.RANK[target_of_interest] ]]+Age+Gender + ORdate_year, data = TEMP.DF)
    coxplot = coxph(Surv(TEMP.DF[,eptime], event) ~ strata(TEMP.DF[[ TRAITS.TARGET.RANK[target_of_interest] ]])+Age+Gender + ORdate_year, data = TEMP.DF)

    plot(survfit(coxplot), main = paste0("Cox proportional hazard of [",ep,"] per [",eptime,"]."),
         # ylim = c(0.2, 1), xlim = c(0,3), col = c("#595A5C", "#DB003F", "#1290D9"),
         ylim = c(0, 1), xlim = c(0,3), col = c("#DB003F", "#1290D9"),
         lty = c(1,2), lwd = 2,
         ylab = "Suvival probability", xlab = "FU time [years]",
         mark.time = FALSE, axes = FALSE, bty = "n")
    legend("topright",
           c("low", "high"),
           title = paste0("",TRAITS.TARGET.RANK[target_of_interest],""),
           col = c("#DB003F", "#1290D9"),
           lty = c(1,2), lwd = 2,
           bty = "n")
    axis(side = 1, at = seq(0, 3, by = 1))
    axis(side = 2, at = seq(0, 1, by = 0.2))
    dev.copy2pdf(file = paste0(COX_loc,"/",
                               Today,".AERNAseurat_meta.Cox.",ep,".2G.",
                               # Today,".AERNASE.clin.targets.Cox.",ep,".4G.",
                               TRAITS.TARGET.RANK[target_of_interest],".MODEL1.pdf"), height = 12, width = 10, onefile = TRUE)
    show(summary(cox))

    cat(paste0("\n   > writing the Cox-regression fashizzle to Excel...\n"))

    COX.results.TEMP <- data.frame(matrix(NA, ncol = 12, nrow = 0))
    COX.results.TEMP[1,] = COX.STAT(cox, "AERNAseurat_meta", ep, TRAITS.TARGET.RANK[target_of_interest])
    COX.results = rbind(COX.results, COX.results.TEMP)
    saveRDS(survfit(coxplot), paste0(COX_loc,"/",
                               Today,".AERNAseurat_meta.Cox.",ep,".2G.",
                               # Today,".AERNASE.clin.targets.Cox.",ep,".4G.",
                               TRAITS.TARGET.RANK[target_of_interest],".MODEL1.cox_survfit_object.rds"))

  }
}

cat("- Edit the column names...\n")
colnames(COX.results) = c("Dataset", "Outcome", "CpG",
                          "Beta", "s.e.m.",
                          "HR", "low95CI", "up95CI",
                          "Z-value", "P-value", "SampleSize", "N_events")

cat("- Correct the variable types...\n")
COX.results$Beta <- as.numeric(COX.results$Beta)
COX.results$s.e.m. <- as.numeric(COX.results$s.e.m.)
COX.results$HR <- as.numeric(COX.results$HR)
COX.results$low95CI <- as.numeric(COX.results$low95CI)
COX.results$up95CI <- as.numeric(COX.results$up95CI)
COX.results$`Z-value` <- as.numeric(COX.results$`Z-value`)
COX.results$`P-value` <- as.numeric(COX.results$`P-value`)
COX.results$SampleSize <- as.numeric(COX.results$SampleSize)
COX.results$N_events <- as.numeric(COX.results$N_events)

AERNAseurat_meta.COX.results <- COX.results

# Save the data
cat("- Writing results to Excel-file...\n")
head.style <- createStyle(textDecoration = "BOLD")
write.xlsx(AERNAseurat_meta.COX.results,
           file = paste0(OUT_loc, "/",Today,".AERNAseurat_meta.Cox.2G.MODEL1.xlsx"),
           creator = "Sander W. van der Laan",
           sheetName = "Results", headerStyle = head.style,
           rowNames = FALSE, colNames = TRUE, overwrite = TRUE)

# Removing intermediates
cat("- Removing intermediate files...\n")
rm(TEMP.DF, target_of_interest, fit, cox, coxplot, COX.results, COX.results.TEMP, head.style, AERNAseurat_meta.COX.results)
```

##### Model 2

```{r Cox-regression Analysis: MODEL 2}
# Set up a dataframe to receive results
COX.results <- data.frame(matrix(NA, ncol = 12, nrow = 0))

# Looping over each target_of_interest/endpoint/time combination
for (i in 1:length(times)){
  eptime = times[i]
  ep = endpoints[i]
  cat(paste0("* Analyzing the effect of plaque target-of-interest on [",ep,"].\n"))
  cat(" - creating temporary SE for this work.\n")
  TEMP.DF = as.data.frame(AERNAseurat_meta_cox)
  cat(" - making a 'Surv' object and adding this to temporary dataframe.\n")
  TEMP.DF$event <- as.integer(TEMP.DF[,ep])
  #as.integer(TEMP.DF[,ep] == "Excluded")

  TEMP.DF$y <- Surv(time = TEMP.DF[,eptime], event = TEMP.DF$event)
  cat(" - making strata of each of the plaque target-of-interest and start survival analysis.\n")
  
  for (target_of_interest in 1:length(TRAITS.TARGET.RANK)){
    cat(paste0("   > processing [",TRAITS.TARGET.RANK[target_of_interest],"]; ",target_of_interest," out of ",length(TRAITS.TARGET.RANK)," target-of-interest.\n"))
    # splitting into two groups
    TEMP.DF[[ TRAITS.TARGET.RANK[target_of_interest] ]] <- cut2(TEMP.DF[,TRAITS.TARGET.RANK[target_of_interest]], g = 2)
    cat(paste0("   > cross tabulation of ",TRAITS.TARGET.RANK[target_of_interest],"-stratum.\n"))
    show(table(TEMP.DF[[ TRAITS.TARGET.RANK[target_of_interest] ]]))
    
    cat(paste0("\n   > fitting the model for ",TRAITS.TARGET.RANK[target_of_interest],"-stratum.\n"))
    fit <- survfit(as.formula(paste0("y ~ ", TRAITS.TARGET.RANK[target_of_interest])), data = TEMP.DF)
    
    cat(paste0("\n   > make a Kaplan-Meier-shizzle...\n"))
    # make Kaplan-Meier curve and save it
    show(ggsurvplot(fit, data = TEMP.DF,
                    palette = c("#DB003F", "#1290D9"),
                    # palete = c("F59D10", "#DB003F", "#49A01D", "#1290D9"),
                    linetype = c(1,2),
                    # linetype = c(1,2,3,4),
                    # conf.int = FALSE, conf.int.fill = "#595A5C", conf.int.alpha = 0.1,
                    pval = FALSE, pval.method = FALSE, pval.size = 4,
                    risk.table = TRUE, risk.table.y.text = FALSE, tables.y.text.col = TRUE, fontsize = 4,
                    censor = FALSE,
                    legend = "right",
                    legend.title = paste0("",TRAITS.TARGET.RANK[target_of_interest],""),
                    legend.labs = c("low", "high"),
                    title = paste0("Risk of ",ep,""), xlab = "Time [years]", font.main = c(16, "bold", "black")))
    dev.copy2pdf(file = paste0(COX_loc,"/",
                               Today,".AERNAseurat_meta.survival.",ep,".2G.",
                               TRAITS.TARGET.RANK[target_of_interest],".pdf"), width = 12, height = 10, onefile = FALSE)

    cat(paste0("\n   > perform the Cox-regression fashizzle and plot it...\n"))
    ### Do Cox-regression and plot it
    
    ### MODEL 2 adjusted for age, sex, hypertension, diabetes, smoking, LDL-C levels, lipid-lowering drugs, antiplatelet drugs, eGFR, BMI, history of CVD, level of stenosis
    cox = coxph(Surv(TEMP.DF[,eptime], event) ~ TEMP.DF[[ TRAITS.TARGET.RANK[target_of_interest] ]]+Age + Gender + ORdate_year + Hypertension.composite + DiabetesStatus + SmokerStatus + Med.Statin.LLD + Med.all.antiplatelet + GFR_MDRD + BMI + MedHx_CVD + stenose, data = TEMP.DF)
    coxplot = coxph(Surv(TEMP.DF[,eptime], event) ~ strata(TEMP.DF[[ TRAITS.TARGET.RANK[target_of_interest] ]])+Age + Gender + ORdate_year + Hypertension.composite + DiabetesStatus + SmokerStatus + Med.Statin.LLD + Med.all.antiplatelet + GFR_MDRD + BMI + MedHx_CVD + stenose, data = TEMP.DF)

  
    plot(survfit(coxplot), main = paste0("Cox proportional hazard of [",ep,"] per [",eptime,"]."),
         # ylim = c(0.2, 1), xlim = c(0,3), col = c("#595A5C", "#DB003F", "#1290D9"),
         ylim = c(0, 1), xlim = c(0,3), col = c("#DB003F", "#1290D9"),
         lty = c(1,2), lwd = 2,
         ylab = "Suvival probability", xlab = "FU time [years]",
         mark.time = FALSE, axes = FALSE, bty = "n")
    legend("topright",
           c("low", "high"),
           title = paste0("",TRAITS.TARGET.RANK[target_of_interest],""),
           col = c("#DB003F", "#1290D9"),
           lty = c(1,2), lwd = 2,
           bty = "n")
    axis(side = 1, at = seq(0, 3, by = 1))
    axis(side = 2, at = seq(0, 1, by = 0.2))
    dev.copy2pdf(file = paste0(COX_loc,"/",
                               Today,".AERNAseurat_meta.Cox.",ep,".2G.",
                               # Today,".AERNASE.clin.targets.Cox.",ep,".4G.",
                               TRAITS.TARGET.RANK[target_of_interest],".MODEL2.pdf"), height = 12, width = 10, onefile = TRUE)
    saveRDS(survfit(coxplot), paste0(COX_loc,"/",
                               Today,".AERNAseurat_meta.Cox.",ep,".2G.",
                               # Today,".AERNASE.clin.targets.Cox.",ep,".4G.",
                               TRAITS.TARGET.RANK[target_of_interest],".MODEL2.cox_survfit_object.rds"))

    show(summary(cox))

    cat(paste0("\n   > writing the Cox-regression fashizzle to Excel...\n"))

    COX.results.TEMP <- data.frame(matrix(NA, ncol = 12, nrow = 0))
    COX.results.TEMP[1,] = COX.STAT(cox, "AERNAseurat_meta", ep, TRAITS.TARGET.RANK[target_of_interest])
    COX.results = rbind(COX.results, COX.results.TEMP)

  }
}
```
